x: Bridger, Heather, Thaxter, Roberts, Doubleday, Snell, and others, supporting Bert Clayton, our Eastleigh member, who may win the individual title, is certainly a team of possibilities.
Our third man, in 18th position, was Harry Thaxter. He completed the course in 9 hr. 11 min. 7 sec., and so gained a first-class standard medal.
Harry Thaxter and Charlie Speechley had a ding-dong battle down Lauriston Road for second place, Thaxter gaining the verdict by a very small margin.

Clayton, Heather, Roberts, Thaxter, Doubleday, Bridger, Goold, Elliott, East, Snell and others have great potentialities, and with conscientious, steady training, we may expect a team which will represent the Club with credit.

These two were still leading at the top of the hills, with Roberts leading Thaxter and Doubleday for third place. Going round the common again, Heather was a few yards in front, but there was little to choose between them when the hills were tackled again.
A gallant but unavailing effort by Harry Thaxter over the last mile reduced the margin to two points, but could not displace Surrey Walking Club, whose team rose to the occasion splendidly.

In this he was nominated as a "B" team man but was able to assist our fourth "A" team man, Harry Thaxter, to complete a Belgrave team win; and was content to finish in 17th position himself, following Thaxter in.
